text:
maria: FYI nightly perf gate failed on kvcache+batching workload — p50 latency up ~7% vs baseline. CI job perf-ci/nightly-1936 flagged it at 04:00 UTC. Can someone pick this up?

perf-bot: Automatic perf gate report attached.
- Job: perf-ci/nightly-1936
- Diff: +7.1% p50, +3% p95
- Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/ci/1936000456/{nsys.tar.gz,perfetto.json,summary.html}
- Trace link: https://perf.redwood/internal/1936000456

josh: on it. do we know which commit landed before the run?

maria: gated commit is 0f3a9e2 — rolled kernel-selection tweak and a KV cache change in the same PR (PR#2891).

alex: looking at the nsys capture now. quick scan shows an extra memcpy around kernel A->B transition. kernel selection ended up using cuBlas-based matmul for seq<=64 instead of our optimized fused-kernel.

alex: perfetto shows repeated small kernels with <1ms gaps causing less efficient occupancy. timeline: https://perf.redwood/internal/1936000456/timeline

nisha: can you paste the nsys summary? curious about SM utilization and achieved occupancy.

alex: paste:```nvidia Nsight Systems Summary:
Total GPU Time: 1.23s
Kernel A (fused_attn): 0.54s occupancy 72%
Kernel B (matmul_cublas): 0.43s occupancy 38%
Memcpy DeviceToDevice: 0.08s
Kernel C (kv_write): 0.18s occupancy 60%
```

alex: notable: Kernel B is both slower and underutilized. earlier baseline used Kernel A variant for that codepath and had contiguous KV caching that avoided D2D memcpy.

josh: so two hypotheses: 1) kernel selection heuristic chose wrong matmul variant, 2) KV cache path introduced extra copies. which is the regressor?

maria: PR#2891 touched both. Need to isolate. plan: rerun the nightly profiler with kernel-selection rollback and with KV cache change toggled off. two CI runs in parallel.

perf-bot: Triggered jobs:
- perf-ci/nightly-1936-a (kernel-selection=rollback) -> queued
- perf-ci/nightly-1936-b (kvcache=old-behavior) -> queued
Artifacts will be uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/ci/1936000456/variants/{a,b}/

nisha: good. also add a perfetto capture of the host timeline around batch formation — I suspect batching heuristics added micro-batching. include env var REDWOOD_BATCH_DEBUG=1.

alex: command I'm running locally to fetch and inspect trace:```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-perf/ci/1936000456/nsys.tar.gz ./ && tar -xzf nsys.tar.gz && nsight-sys ./report.qdrep
```

josh: if variant-a clears the gate, we should revert kernel-selection change and open a follow-up to rework selection logic with more robust tests.

maria: agreed. can someone add a short CI gating test that runs a representative request pattern and asserts p50 within +2%? even a pared-down microbenchmark would help.

nisha: I'll add a microbenchmark to perf-tests/kv-batch-smoke and wire it into the nightly perf gate as a fast pre-check.

alex: small note: when inspecting perfetto, see host-side delay ~6ms while KV fetch finishes — that lines up with D2D copies. KV cache path likely doing an extra staging buffer.

josh: thanks. I'll watch the two variant runs and post diffs when available. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Variant results posted:
- variant-a: p50 -0.3% (passes)
- variant-b: p50 +6.9% (fails)
Diff dashboard: https://perf.redwood/diff/1936000456/

maria: that's pretty conclusive — kernel-selection change caused the regression. rolling back selection tweak now, will open a follow-up to redesign selection rules and add CV-like tests for small-seq matmuls.

josh: cool. once rollback lands, let's run a smoke perf job in CI to confirm and then close the incident.

nisha: added perf-test and a brief doc in docs/perf/kv-batching.md describing the expected kernel mapping and why staging buffers are bad for small seqs.

maria: awesome work team. closing thread once rollback validated. :tada:
